results.problem: DGEMM emulation with INT8 on Intel Arc/Xe2
results.quote: On an Intel Arc Pro B60 (24GB) the emulated DGEMM reaches 17.3, 12.1 and 9.3 TFLOP/s with s=8, 12 and 16 moduli at N=8192, and up to 21.1 TFLOP/s overall, i.e. 12-28× the native FP64 DGEMM of the same board; 75-90% of the run time is spent in INT8 GEMM at ≈95% of its attainable rate.

results.problem: ZGEMM emulation with INT8 on Intel Arc/Xe2
results.quote: The emulated ZGEMM, which uses the 3M form exactly in integer arithmetic, reaches up to 27.4 TFLOP/s and is 13.7-17.8× faster than native ZGEMM for N≥4096 at s=16.

results.bound: s\ge 16\ \text{correctly rounded (well-scaled)};\ s=20\text{--}24\ \text{extended-width path (wide exponent range)}
results.quote: With s≥16 the results are correctly rounded for well-scaled inputs and, using an extended-width residue path (s=20-24), also for inputs with wide exponent ranges, whereas native DGEMM on GPU or CPU rounds only 2-13% of the entries correctly.

results.problem: Ozaki scheme I vs. scheme II on INT8 engine
results.quote: At comparable accuracy, scheme I needs 36-45 INT8 GEMMs where scheme II needs 15-16, and it is 2.3-2.9 times slower ( 15, Figure 5).
